senses.gloss: To officially end a rule, a ban, or a restriction.
examples: The governor plans to *lift* the mask requirement next week.
The city *lifted* the curfew after three quiet nights.
Sanctions have been *lifted* on most farm imports.

senses.gloss: To copy someone else's words or work without permission.
examples: He *lifts* his best jokes from old sitcoms.
Reviewers found that she had *lifted* whole paragraphs from a blog.
The melody was *lifted* straight from a 1970s hit.

senses.gloss: To click the like button on a post, a photo, or a comment.
examples: *Like* the video if you want to see more of them.
She *liked* my photo but never left a comment.
The post has been *liked* forty thousand times.

senses.gloss: To stand or be arranged in a row along something.
senses.ru: стоять вдоль, выстраиваться вдоль; тянуться вдоль
examples: Oak trees *line* both sides of the street.
Fans *lined* the sidewalk for six blocks.
The hallway is *lined* with family photos.

senses.gloss: To do what someone tells or advises you to do.
examples: The kids never *listen* to their babysitter.
We all warned him, but he wasn't *listening* to anybody.
If he had *listened* to his doctor, he would not be in the hospital.

senses.gloss: To bring a page, a program, or a file into a computer so that it can be used.
examples: The site takes forever to *load* on my phone.
The game *loaded* in under ten seconds.
The map is still *loading*.

senses.gloss: To put ammunition into a gun, or film into a camera.
examples: He *loads* the shotgun before dawn.
She *loaded* the camera with black-and-white film.
The rifle was already *loaded*.

senses.gloss: To put or build something in a particular place.
examples: They plan to *locate* the new plant near the river.
The company *located* its headquarters in Austin.
The restrooms are *located* at the back of the store.

senses.gloss: To become fixed firmly in one position so that it cannot move.
examples: Push the shelf down until the brackets *lock* into place.
The brakes *locked* and the car slid sideways.
The tray table is *locked* in the upright position.

senses.gloss: To become stuck firmly in a place.
examples: A popcorn kernel can *lodge* between your teeth.
The bullet *lodged* in his shoulder.
A splinter had *lodged* under her nail.

senses.gloss: To make a complaint or a claim formally to an authority.
examples: You can *lodge* a complaint with the state board.
Three neighbors *lodged* protests with the city.
A formal appeal has been *lodged*.

senses.gloss: To cut down the trees in an area for timber.
senses.ru: вырубать лес, заготавливать лес; вести лесозаготовки
examples: Crews still *log* parts of the national forest.
They *logged* this whole hillside in the 1950s.
Most of the valley has already been *logged*.

senses.gloss: To repeat over and over from the beginning without stopping.
senses.ru: повторяться по кругу, зацикливаться; ставить на повтор
examples: The ad *loops* every thirty seconds on the screen.
We *looped* the same song for the whole drive.
A ten-second clip was *looping* above the stage.

senses.gloss: To say firmly that something is true, even when other people doubt it.
examples: He *maintains* that he never saw the email.
She *maintained* her innocence through two trials.
They have *maintained* all along that the data is safe.

senses.gloss: To succeed in doing something difficult.
examples: Somehow we *manage* to pay the rent every month.
She *managed* to finish the report before midnight.
He has *managed* to avoid the subject all week.

senses.gloss: To use clever or indirect moves to get into the position you want.
examples: He knows how to *maneuver* around the board's objections.
She *maneuvered* herself into the top job in two years.
They spent the spring *maneuvering* for the nomination.

senses.gloss: To work something skillfully with your hands or with a tool.
senses.ru: управлять руками, ловко обращаться (с чем-л.); манипулировать (предметом)
examples: Surgeons *manipulate* the instruments through three small cuts.
She *manipulated* the joystick with one hand.
The robot arm is *manipulated* from the next room.

senses.gloss: To invent something false, such as an excuse or evidence.
examples: Don't *manufacture* an excuse — just tell them the truth.
The article claims that agents *manufactured* the evidence.
The whole scandal was *manufactured* by a rival campaign.

senses.gloss: To walk somewhere quickly and with angry determination.
senses.ru: решительно идти, решительно направиться; врываться, ворваться
examples: Don't just *march* into his office without knocking.
She *marched* straight up to the manager and demanded a refund.
He came *marching* down the hall waving the bill.

senses.gloss: To be the sign that an important event, change, or stage has happened.
examples: Today's vote *marks* a turning point for the company.
The 1969 landing *marked* the end of the space race.
This election has *marked* a real shift in the state.

senses.gloss: To do something special to celebrate or remember an occasion.
examples: How do you plan to *mark* your tenth anniversary?
The town *marked* Memorial Day with a parade.
The date is *marked* every year with a moment of silence.

senses.gloss: To be equal to something, or to do as well as it.
examples: No other store can *match* that price.
He *matched* the world record on his second try.
The company has *matched* every dollar she put into her 401(k).

senses.gloss: When a bond, a loan, or an investment matures, it reaches the date when it must be paid.
senses.ru: наступать (о сроке погашения); погашаться, быть погашенным
examples: The bond will *mature* in ten years.
Her CD *matured* last month, so she reinvested it.
By the time the policy has *matured*, it will be worth double.

senses.gloss: To be a particular size, length, or amount.
examples: The kitchen *measures* twelve feet by fifteen.
The trout *measured* almost two feet.
The crack must *measure* an inch across.

senses.gloss: To move data, software, or users from one system to another.
examples: We *migrate* the last accounts tonight.
They *migrated* the whole database to the cloud.
All the old files have been *migrated* to the new server.

senses.gloss: To get as much money or advantage out of something as you possibly can.
examples: Some comedians *milk* a joke until it dies.
He *milked* the injury for two extra weeks off.
They are *milking* the story for every click it is worth.

senses.gloss: To look, sound, or behave very much like something else.
senses.ru: имитировать, воспроизводить; напоминать (по виду, по действию)
examples: The new material *mimics* real leather.
Her symptoms *mimicked* the flu for a week.
The software is *mimicking* the hiss of an old tape machine.

senses.gloss: To take care of someone or something for a short time.
examples: Could you *mind* the baby while I run to the store?
She *minded* the front desk during lunch.
He has been *minding* his neighbor's dog all week.

senses.gloss: To mix together so that the separate parts are hard to tell apart.
examples: Smoke and fog *mingle* over the valley on cold mornings.
The smell of coffee *mingled* with fresh bread.
Cheers were *mingling* with the sound of the band.

senses.gloss: To make something seem less important or less serious than it really is.
examples: Don't *minimize* what she went through.
The company *minimized* the risks in its first statement.
He has a habit of *minimizing* his own achievements.

senses.gloss: To be very similar to something else, or to reflect it closely.
examples: The state numbers *mirror* the national trend.
His career *mirrored* his father's almost exactly.
The mood in the room was *mirrored* in the voting.

senses.gloss: To fail to hit, catch, or reach something you aimed at.
senses.ru: промахиваться, промахнуться; не попадать, не попасть
examples: Aim lower or you will *miss* the target again.
He *missed* the free throw that would have tied the game.
The ball flew past, *missing* the goal by an inch.

senses.gloss: To arrive too late for something, or to fail to be there for it.
examples: Hurry up or we will *miss* the train.
I *missed* the first ten minutes of the movie.
He has *missed* three classes this month.

senses.gloss: To fail to notice or understand something.
senses.ru: не замечать, не заметить; упускать, упустить (из виду)
examples: It is easy to *miss* the turn in the dark.
You *missed* the point of the whole story.
I must have *missed* that email.

senses.gloss: To show a way of behaving so that other people can copy it.
senses.ru: показывать пример, подавать пример; демонстрировать образец
examples: Parents *model* the manners they want to see.
The coach *modeled* the move slowly, step by step.
Teachers are *modeling* the behavior they expect in class.

senses.gloss: To be in charge of a discussion or an online group, keeping it fair and within the rules.
examples: A local anchor will *moderate* tonight's debate.
She *moderated* the panel at the conference.
Volunteers have been *moderating* the forum for years.

senses.gloss: In grammar, to add meaning to another word by describing or limiting it.
examples: Adjectives *modify* nouns.
In this sentence the adverb *modifies* the verb.
That phrase is *modifying* the whole clause, not just the noun.

senses.gloss: To shape the way someone's character or opinions develop.
examples: Good coaches *mold* more than athletes.
Her years abroad *molded* the way she sees this country.
He was *molded* by a very strict upbringing.

senses.gloss: To wipe sweat or water off your face or skin with a cloth.
examples: He *mops* his forehead between rounds.
She *mopped* her face with a paper towel.
The old man sat *mopping* his brow in the heat.
